chunks: "A man may worship Allah for forty years, yet he does not obey Him in wudu (ablution), because he washes what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded to be wiped."

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً: for forty years, indicating a long duration
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One being worshipped and obeyed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.بِمَسْحِهِ: by wiping it, meaning what is prescribed to be wiped in wudu

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say a person may worship for forty years yet not obey Allah in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teaches that long worship is not sufficient if one fails to follow Allah’s command correctly in wudu (ablution). The hadith emphasizes precise obedience in ritual purity, especially regarding wiping rather than washing where Allah has prescribed wiping.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.73 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"A man may worship Allah (swt) for forty years but does not truly obey Him in wudu (ablution) because he washes what Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to wipe."
